C0.quote: axiomatic characterization of a class of certification methods
C0.note: Axiomatic study of approval voting and proportional threshold aggregation of binary opinions into collective decisions.

C1.quote: provide an axiomatic characterization of the approval voting method

C2.1.quote: an evaluation profile on (N, X) collects the evaluations of the electorate

C2.2.quote: each agent i ∈ N can either approve of an option x ∈ X or disapprove
C2.2.note: Binary approve/disapprove evaluations, equivalent to approval sets. The paper also mentions 'binary opinions'.

C2.3.quote: consistency properties across populations and profiles of binary opinions
C2.3.note: Refers to 'opinions' and 'negative opinion' of voters. Weak: 'opinions' is used interchangeably with the evaluations that are the input.

C2.4.quote: Each option is evaluated by the agents.
C2.4.note: Evaluations/opinions are the input to the rule; there is no statement about submission or misreporting.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notion for voters is used.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is used only in reference titles, not in the paper's model.

C5.1.note: Only axioms are evaluated. 'Pareto consistency' is a structural axiom on inputs, not a welfare criterion.

VOT.note: Agents only provide evaluations as an input to the rule; no agent action is modelled as an agent choice.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: helpful to understand an important distinction between rules offering acceptable outcomes
Proportional threshold methods and the approval voting method serve substantially different purposes

C9.1.note: Claims about which situations suit which method (certification vs competitive selection), and about real institutions such as impeachment.

C9.2.note: The claims about suitable use follow from the axioms, which are normative, plus the claim that the axioms are desirable. No assumptions about strategic behaviour, information or held attitudes are needed, and none are stated. The suitability claim is only loosely tied to the formal results, so this is somewhat uncertain.

C10.1.note: No statement of a procedural reading.
